title: DPIIT Startup Advisory Council gets founders of Zoho, Lenskart, OYO, Groww, Zepto, Minimalist on board
summary: DPIIT appoints founders of Zoho, Zepto and Oyer to Startup Advisory Council
detailed: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has formed the National Startup Advisory Council, comprised of entrepreneurs from startups and unicorns, venture capitalists, industrialists, policy makers, academicians and trade associations to advise the government on policies that would help improve the startup ecosystem in the country.

The National Startup Advisory Council comprises of Sridhar Vembu, founder of Zoho Corporation, Lenskart CEO Peyush Bansal, OYO Founder Ritesh Agarwal, Groww COO Harsh Jain, CFO of Zepto Ramesh Bafna and Minimalist co-founder Mohit Yadav among others who are well-known in their respective sectors.

This includes Pawan Kumar Chandana, the co-founder and CEO of Skyroot Aerospace; Kushagra Srivastava, the founder of Chakr Innovation; Mohit Yadav, the co-founder of Minimalist; Ramesh Bafna, the CFO of Zepto; and Peyush Bansal, the CEO of Lenskart.

Other nominees to this council include Ritesh Agarwal, the founder of OYO; Harsh Jain, the COO of Groww; Vivek Raghavan, the co-founder of Sarvam AI; and Captain Parashar Nikunj, the founder and CEO of Sagar Defence Engineering.
sentences: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has formed the National Startup Advisory Council, comprised of entrepreneurs from startups and unicorns, venture capitalists, industrialists, policy makers, academicians and trade associations to advise the government on policies that would help improve the startup ecosystem in the country.

The National Startup Advisory Council comprises of Sridhar Vembu, founder of Zoho Corporation, Lenskart CEO Peyush Bansal, OYO Founder Ritesh Agarwal, Groww COO Harsh Jain, CFO of Zepto Ramesh Bafna and Minimalist co-founder Mohit Yadav among others who are well-known in their respective sectors.

The formation of the council comes with the aim to bring together stakeholders in the startup community to discuss the measures needed to foster innovation, sustainable economic development and create jobs on a mass scale.
According to the memorandum issued by DPIIT, the Central Government has appointed non-official members representing various stakeholders in the council.
Their term would be two years or until further order, whichever is earlier.
The venture capital and investors section comprises Prashanth Prakash from Accel, Gopal Srinivasan of TVS Capital Funds, and Rajan Anandan of Peak XV Partners.

Other members on the council include industry leaders and policymakers such as Anita George, the CEO of ProsperETE, and independent director at Tata Sons and Piramal Enterprises; former Secretary, Biotechnology, Renu Swarup; founder of Nishith Desai Associates, Nishith Desai; and co-founder of iSPIRT, the Indian Software Product Industry RoundTable, Sharad Sharma.
Also nominated is Debjani Ghosh who is a Distinguished Fellow of NITI Aayog and the chief architect of NITI Frontier Tech Hub and former President of NASSCOM.
Others include Sunil Kant Munjal of Hero Enterprise, and astronaut Captain Shubhanshu Shukla.

Startup founders from consumer, fintech and deeptech sectors
This startup board covers companies involved in consumer goods, fintech, artificial intelligence, aerospace, defence technology, and innovations focused on sustainability.

This includes Pawan Kumar Chandana, the co-founder and CEO of Skyroot Aerospace; Kushagra Srivastava, the founder of Chakr Innovation; Mohit Yadav, the co-founder of Minimalist; Ramesh Bafna, the CFO of Zepto; and Peyush Bansal, the CEO of Lenskart.

Other nominees to this council include Ritesh Agarwal, the founder of OYO; Harsh Jain, the COO of Groww; Vivek Raghavan, the co-founder of Sarvam AI; and Captain Parashar Nikunj, the founder and CEO of Sagar Defence Engineering.

The council also includes representation from academia and institutions with IIT Madras director Prof V Kamakoti and Aravind Chinchure, who is the founder and CEO of QLeap Academy and Deshpande Foundation’s board member being amongst those who have been named.

In terms of representation from the banking and investment facilitation eco-system, the managing director of State Bank of India as well as the managing director and CEO of Invest India have been included.
Further, there will also be representation from the industry bodies with nominees from FICCI and ASSOCHAM.
According to the memorandum, FICCI nominee will be nominated from their relevant startup team while that of ASSOCHAM would be chosen by its President.

This is all part of the efforts of the government to enhance the startup eco-system where innovation, access to capital, entrepreneurship and employment generation are some of the other aspects that have been laid down in the memorandum.
The order does not include any information about the meeting schedule or agenda of the council for its very first sitting.
However, it does state that the nominated non-official members would remain on the council for two years or till further orders, whichever is earlier.
